Subject: Private hostnames: cert delegation, proxying, and egress TLS options

Daniel / CloudOps team —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We want to lock the approach for TLS and DNS for the private endpoints in your VPC (acme.private.redwood-acme.com and *.svc.acme). There are three pragmatic options we typically propose; I wanted to capture them here and get your preference and constraints so we can update the runbook: see attached quick checklist.

Summary of options (high level):
1) Customer-managed termination (preferred for regulated workloads) — your infra owns the certs (Vault/PKI or Cloud CA), terminates TLS in the VPC/ingress, Redwood speaks mTLS or mutual-auth to that endpoint.
2) Redwood-managed edge proxy with private endpoint mapping — we terminate TLS on our edge inside a private peering, we maintain certs, and route to your private service over encrypted link (TLS or plain, per policy).
3) Passthrough to customer NLB (TLS passthrough) — we SNI pass-through to your NLB and you handle certs entirely. Better for zero-touch cert ownership but loses application-level visibility at the proxy.

Key constraints we need from you:
- Do you have a cert automation mechanism (ACME with DNS-01, Vault PKI, or manual uploads)?
- Is there any policy that forbids third-party cert management (i.e., can Redwood hold private certs for the acme.private namespace)?
- Which DNS provider manages the internal split-horizon zone? Can we provision CNAMEs or delegation records?

Attached: cert-delegation-checklist.pdf (stub).

If you can reply with preferences and any blocker items, we’ll draft a short runbook and propose a handoff call next week.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor

Subject: Re: Private hostnames: cert delegation, proxying, and egress TLS options

Neha —

Thanks for the summary. A few constraints from our side:
- We cannot allow any external party to hold private CA material for prod. For staging/test we could allow Redwood-managed certs but they must be rotated monthly and restricted to non-prod namespaces.
- Our infra uses HashiCorp Vault (internal PKI) for cert issuance and we have an ACME facade for some teams, but it is not reachable outside our VPC.
- DNS: internal split-horizon is handled by our Route53 private zones; we can add CNAMEs but prefer not to give full delegation of the zone.
- We can accept SNI pass-through to our NLB for now, but for prod we want termination inside our cluster with mTLS to the Redwood component.

Questions:
- If we do customer-managed termination, can Redwood support certificate renewals via Ops-managed cert uploads (we can push to a secure S3 + signed webhook)?
- For Redwood-managed proxy in staging, what level of logging/PII filtering do you support? We need to be sure no sensitive payloads are persisted.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call — I can loop our CloudOps partner (support@cloudops.io) for implementation details.

—Daniel

Subject: Re: Private hostnames: cert delegation, proxying, and egress TLS options

+1 on the constraints. A few technical notes we should call out for the runbook and for Acme:

- Cert acquisition options we support:
  * ACME (DNS-01) — requires Redwood to be able to create DNS TXT records in the customer zone OR for the customer to provision the records (automation preferred).
  * Manual upload — customer uploads cert+chain+key to a secure endpoint (we store in KMS-backed secret store).
  * External PKI integration — support for Vault PKI issuing short-lived certs via a signed CSR workflow.

- DNS pattern recommendations:
  * Use split-horizon private zone (e.g., acme.private) and add aliased records for staging/prod: e.g., staging-api.acme.private -> redwood-edge-staging.internal; prod-api.acme.private -> <customer-nlb> (SNI pass-through) or -> redwood-edge-prod if agreed.
  * Avoid delegating the whole zone; prefer CNAME/CNAME-delegation per service to limit blast radius.

- TLS termination tradeoffs:
  * Customer termination gives full control for audit/compliance and is strongly preferred for prod. Redwood can validate mTLS client certs from your ingress; mutual-auth provides good proof-of-origin.
  * Redwood-managed termination lowers ops burden for Acme but requires a contract change: Redwood must hold certs for that namespace (we can put them in a customer-specific KMS using BYOK model). For regulated tenants we can scope to non-prod only.
  * Passthrough retains cert op ownership but reduces protocol visibility; it complicates tracing and per-route telemetry.

- Operational items:
  * Cert rotation window and TTL — recommend short-lived certs (90 days) and an automation plan.
  * OCSP/CRL access — ensure revocation info is reachable from any termination point.

I'll draft the technical section of the runbook with these patterns. If Acme can confirm whether they can push certs to an S3 bucket + signed webhook, we can design the upload flow.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private hostnames: cert delegation, proxying, and egress TLS options

A couple of practical points from the cert-ops side:

- If Acme runs Vault PKI, we can integrate via an automated CSR workflow: Redwood creates CSR, Acme's Vault signs and returns cert. That preserves key ownership on their side if we do not require the private key to leave their VPC. Works well for prod.

- For staging where you said monthly rotation is acceptable, we suggest using Redwood-managed certs with automated rotation and a scoped retention policy (no request/response bodies logged, truncated metadata only). We will include an option to redact headers/bodies for sensitive routes.

- SAN planning: confirm the exact FQDNs you will expose. Wildcards are fine but ACLs and issuer policies might block wildcard issuance depending on your Vault policies.

- ACME/DNS: since your DNS is private Route53, if you prefer ACME we have two options: (A) you run a short-lived ACME challenge runner in your VPC that we trigger via the signed webhook to create TXT records, or (B) you grant a scoped role so our ACME agent can write DNS TXT records. Option (A) is lower trust.

I'm attaching a skeleton runbook table in the shared Drive (link in metadata) and will add the CSR flow diagram.

—Chloe
Platform Infra, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — summary and decisions to proceed:

1) Staging: Redwood-managed edge termination is acceptable. We will host staging certs (monthly rotation). Redwood will redact request bodies and preserve only route metadata for logs.

2) Production: customer-managed termination inside Acme VPC. We will integrate via the Vault CSR pattern so keys never leave Acme's trust boundary. Redwood will request CSR, Acme's Vault will sign and return certs. If Vault cannot support a signed CSR flow for any reason, fallback is an S3+signed-webhook upload mechanism.

3) DNS: Acme will provide specific FQDNs for staging and prod. We will avoid delegating the entire private zone; instead we will use CNAME aliases per service.

4) Next steps: Marcus to schedule the 7/22 handoff (30 mins) to wire the CSR flow and agree on runbook checklist items (INF-3421). Chloe/Karthik to finalize the runbook sections on rotation and OCSP.

Daniel — can you confirm the FQDN list and whether your Vault can perform CSR signing by EOD 7/21? If not, confirm we can use the S3 upload fallback.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
